oracles.rationale:
🏛️ EnergyPlus is the heat-balance solver ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 140 is itself written around, which is what makes it a QUALIFYING reference for this subset's SIMULATION capability rather than a second opinion: the standard's §5.2 building-envelope cases are the acceptance instrument for exactly the physics `🔨️modules/⚡️simulation/⚙️engine` implements. The reference runs out of process — `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🔋️energy/🔮️oracles/🏃️execution/🐍️.py` reads the same `🔋️model.json` the engine reads, translates it through honeybee to an OpenStudio model and an IDF, runs the EnergyPlus binary, and reads the SQLite output back. It imports nothing from the Rust it judges. The toolchain is provisioned zero-touch by that package's `📜️script.ts setup` into `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/⚡️cache/oracles/openstudio-3.11.0-<platform>/` from the pinned, sha256-verified release archive recorded in `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🔋️energy/🔮️oracles/🛠️toolchain/🔣️.json`, so no network access happens during a test run.

INDEPENDENCE. Accounted at the engine-family level: `honeybee-energy`, `honeybee-openstudio` and the `openstudio` bindings are three packages over ONE kernel (EnergyPlus 25.2.0), so this registration is one oracle, not three. It is independent of the sibling `energy-model-1-python-independent` entry, which judges the mutation vocabulary and shares no code with it.

[2026-09-06, W-B — 26/09/06/ENERGY-PLUGIN-END-TO-END] HISTORY, REVERSING THE EARLIER DECLINE. The sibling entry above records, verbatim, a survey that NAMED AND DECLINED EnergyPlus and OpenStudio. That decision is correct for the capability it was made about and is NOT overturned: no third party reads or writes `s.energy.model`'s own `.dsl.semio` carrier, so the MUTATION capability `energy-model-1-mutate` still has no qualifying third-party reference and still rests on the in-repository second implementation. What the decline did not consider is that this subset carries a second, physically-typed capability — simulating the `Model` it persists — and for THAT capability EnergyPlus is not merely available but canonical. This entry therefore reverses the decline for `energy-model-1-simulate` only, and leaves `energy-model-1-mutate`'s standing debt exactly where it was.

EVIDENCE THIS REFERENCE IS ITSELF CORRECT. The runner's `native` mode rebuilds ASHRAE 140 §5.2 cases from the standard's own geometry and layer tables, independently of any semio input. Those results were compared against NREL's own published BESTEST-GSR run (`results/workflow_results.csv`, OpenStudio 3.11.0 / EnergyPlus 25.2.0): case 600 annual heating 4324.74 kWh vs NREL 4325, cooling 6044.06 vs 6041.67; case 900 1661.14 / 2498.16 vs 1661.11 / 2491.67; case 600FF free-float −12.5606 °C … 63.92 °C vs −12.5606 … 63.92; case 900FF 1.2467 … 44.2992 vs 1.24666 … 44.2992. Ten cases agree within 0.4 %. Numbers and method: `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️06/ENERGY-PLUGIN-END-TO-END/📓️w2-oracle-toolchain.md`.

oracles.rationale: ⚡️ The SECOND EnergyPlus route, and deliberately not the same registration as `energyplus-25-2-0-via-honeybee-openstudio`. That entry judges PHYSICS and reaches EnergyPlus through honeybee-energy → honeybee-openstudio → OpenStudio; `📓️w2-oracle-toolchain.md` measures that translation as worth +5.7…+8.1 % of annual cooling all by itself, which means it cannot also be the reference for the DOCUMENT, since a codec fault and a translator fault would be indistinguishable. This entry judges `energy-model-1-io`: the `⚡️epjson` export leaf writes an EnergyPlus 25.2 document with no third party in the path, and two independent references read it — the third-party `jsonschema` validator against EnergyPlus's own 858-object-type `Energy+.schema.epJSON` (shipped inside the same sha256-verified OpenStudio archive), and the `energyplus` binary itself, invoked as `energyplus -a -w <epw> -d <dir> <file.epJSON>`. The results are read from EnergyPlus's own `eplusout.sql` through the Python standard library's `sqlite3` and from the `Zone Information` record in its own `eplusout.eio`, so ladybug is not in this path either — which also keeps the oracle host runnable on the repository's own Python 3.14 interpreter, where the compiled `openstudio` wheel cannot install (that measurement is recorded in `📓️w2-oracle-toolchain.md` §2). The comparison is against the committed `🔮️energyplus.json` the honeybee route produced, at 3 % on annual energy and ±0.5 K on free-float temperature: both numbers come out of the same EnergyPlus 25.2.0 build reading the same simple glazing, so the documented glazing offset is common to both sides and the only thing that can move them apart is the document. No network during execution; the toolchain is provisioned once by `nx run @semio-tech/energy-oracle-py:oracle-setup`.
